comment: What made the class hard was the content, not the professor. He's very kind and a good teacher, but also very direct. He assigns homework for every class, but it's accepted until the day of a test and he only removes one point for late work. The class itself was very difficult and requires a lot of studying before each test.
Dr. Goddu loves his logic. This is one of those subjects that you either get or you don't. Grading is fair and predictable. Homework is time-intensive.

Be prepared to spend 10+ hours a week on homework!! Definitely an interesting class and I would recommend for anyone who can't do math, but it takes a lot of effort and hard work, it's like learning a language. I am proud that I finished the course and Goddu is great, but would not take again. Biggest stressor of my freshman year.

Super hard course. Definitely not like anything I have ever learned before. Dr. Goddu is very accessible in office hours and willing to help if you are struggling. The lack of a textbook is annoying though. Make sure you know people in the class who can send their notes if you miss class (otherwise there's no catching up on what you missed).

Dr. Goddu is very funny, but Phil 251 is a difficult course. I took this as a freshman and it required a lot of effort. Do not go into it expecting an easy A. You will learn a lot, but the course will kick the crap out of you. I practically lived in his office, but he is very available and is willing to explain and re-explain any concepts necessary

Dr. Goddu is a knowledgeable teacher. He assigns homework every day after class, and there are three tests and a final. There is no extra credit, but if you do all the homework, even if wrong, you still get an 8. At first, it was hard to understand, but as class flowed, it all became clearer! Class is mandatory, if not you won't get the homework.

Prof. Goddu is an interesting guy & he is not for everyone. You either get this concept or you don't, if you don't the class is super hard, & requires lots of extra work outside of class to even get a 'B'. Homework can sometimes take hours depending on the concept. You cannot miss class, or you will be super confused b/c there's no textbook.

Dr. Goddu is one of the best professors at UR, but teaches a rather time-consuming and hard class. His office hours were virtually mandatory for me and a lot of extra work was required outside of class to do well. As a professor, he is great, and endearingly awkward sometimes. He's very sharp. Make sure you know what you're getting into, however.

Professor Goddu is like a wizard lol. He's super knowledgeable and gets super excited when teaching. He cares about his students and really wants his students to pass. He's a lenient grader and as long as you keep up with the work you'll be ok. I skipped class a lot and it reflected in my grade.

professor goddu is crazy knowledgeable and a great professor. his class is def not easy but if you put in substantial work, you can do well. also i would heavily recommend going to his office hours, that helped me a lot and he is always happy to help! he is also just a bit of a silly guy :p
Like Goddu, but class is hard and is set up so that if you miss one class, you fall incredibly behind. Class is somewhat fun but hard. It's like doing puzzles.

Professor Goddu is a great logic professor and also just a cool guy. Logic is difficult if it doesn't *click* with you, but he makes most of the components make sense individually. If you need extra help he's always available during office hours. Difficult for me personally, but not a reflection on Professor Goddu's teaching as a whole.

If you need a math credit and want to avoid calc, TAKE THIS! His lectures are very well put together. He's very high energy, and his office hours are super helpful (I go to almost all of them). He goes over the homework at the beginning of class, so you can change answers. Attendance optional, but it's tough to understand if you miss a class.

If you attend class regularly, you will pass this class with no trouble. He is big on partial credit, but isn't always super clear about his grading criteria. He goes over homework at the beginning of every class, and is accessible outside of the classroom. If you are remotely decent at math, this class will be an absolute breeze.

He is very unclear about expectations on papers, so everyone usually gets an 80 or lower. he takes off one percentage point from your final grade for every class you miss (even if the deans are in contact with him). His lectures are really boring and not at all helpful. I don't think I've legitimately learned anything aside from the readings.

Dr. Goddu was a solid professor. I will say that in the beginning, grasping the concept of logic is hard, especially since it's not taught in most high schools, but once you get the hang of it, it gets easier. He does seem a little intimidating and teaches FAST, but he's accessible outside of class and very willing to help.

Dr. Goddu is so smart and he is a great teacher. I enjoyed his classes. He regularly gives homework but they really help you get a better understanding of the topics. Attendance is not mandatory but you wouldn't be able to pass. If you are only considering taking this class for the symbolic reasoning requirement, calculus 1 is easier.
Goddu is a great logic teacher but don't take this course unless you have to for the major. Unnecessarily hard, graded on philosophical stories as if I had written tons of them before
I had him for Symbolic Logic, never quite felt like I 'got' anything that was going on & there was little class time for questions, so it was very frustrating.

Every lecture is like a game. He is clear and precise both in his lectures and expectations. This is an intro class, not hard, but you have to be able to think logically. One downside is Writing Assignments (i.e. logic puzzles). These are a small part of your grade, and hard to do poorly in, but it would be nice to practice them more in class.

He is absolutely the professor to whom I'll feel grateful for enlightening me. He truly knows how to educate. Highly recommend his students to go to his office hour/after class and talk to him. He'll also teach you sth about philosophy per se.  Also if you really want to hone your academic skills, don't miss his class. He'll help you with his best.

I love Dr. Goddu!!! I took him for logic for my math credit and I am so glad I did. He is hilarious in an awkward way and is extremely willing to help students outside of class. His method of teaching is very clear. I happen to understand logic really well, so I find this class pretty easy, but I do know a lot of people who find it very challenging

Goddu is the man. He is incredibly smart and it shows because he is slightly awkward, but he is a very cool person. Very tough grader and the class is super interesting, but it is also super hard. Lots of cool topics covered and it greatly improves your critical writing and thinking skills. Assigns one problem set per week for homework.

This professor was amazing. I agree with the previous reviewer, he does remind me of Robin Williams in a way. The class I took was extremely interesting and challenging. It was hard to get a good grade, but that challenge had me trying harder every day. I would recommend this professor to any first-year student. Take him if you get the chance.

This class was awesome! It was mostly logic puzzles, which were pretty hard. But, if you explain yourself well, you will do well. He kinda reminds me of Robin Williams in a way. The class itself was really fun. It is difficult to get a good grade, but I can say that it has challenged me.

He was a concise teacher and got the job done, never falling behind. He was also really willing to help you during office hours and was clear in his explanations. However, the material is bizarre and the tests are really hard and are not graded on a curve.

He was pretty cool and the class was fun.  Just did logic puzzles for a lot of it.  They were hard but you mostly just needed to be good at explaining.  He was helpful on the essays but they were very challenging.  He lets you rewrite the important one though!

Lovee him! He is a great professor and extremely helpful. He teaches everything during class and does not use a textbook. He does not require attendance, but since he does not use a textbook it is best to go to every class. He is super smart and always willing to help. He is also very funny and makes for a great class!

I love Dr. Goddu-- He is the MAN. Very helpful and was always there when I needed him to review anything. Although the material was hard, his teaching was crystal clear and to the point. There is not a single day wasted in his class, every day COUNTS. I would definitely take another class with him!

Goddu's a tough professor but a good guy.  You have to take this course if you're a philosophy major, so the best advice I have is to try to meet with him frequently because he's very very harsh on the first 5-6 assignments.

Its easy to think of Goddu in class as thinking he's a "god" no pun intended, but whenever I needed help and went to see him during office hours he was the funniest,down to earth prof. I have met. It's hard to dislike him unless you just hate prof. who actually know their stuff when you don't. Take my advice coming from a person struggling.

Other ratings suggest Dr. Goddu is arrogant and enjoys making students feel stupid.  This is completely untrue--says more about the reviewers.  Goddu is brilliant  but completely down to earth/enthusiastic--class is challenging, but he is a very good teacher and makes difficult/esoteric subject approachable.  Take him if you are major/minor!

goddu thinks he is a genius. philosophy of science fiction. knowledge about an area that does not actually exist. his class made me feel stupid and damaged my self esteem. goddu seemed to enjoy my failure it seemed to me. i have since completed undegraduate degree, law school and now embarking on master of law.
Really great professor- will give you all the help you need and keeps class interesting with his unique sense of humor... Extreemly smart- he's probably a genius.

Dr. Goddu is smarter than you...he will never let you forget this the entire time you are in his class.  Maybe you will have a shadow of his genius at solving logic problems, but you probably won't, which is just tough luck for you.

Nature of the class is either you get it or you don't.  If you don't, he'll give you as much help as he can.  If you get it, then the class rocks.  As for him, he's crazy, awesome, fun, and has science fiction all over his office.  Very cool!
Learned a lot and he's really into the class.

Goddu is amazing!!  I loved his class and learned so much - although its hard at times, it has definitely helped me in preparing for the LAST.  He is so so intelligent, but NOT one of those guys who makes you feel below him.  He also has this unique sense of humor and wants everyone to succeed.

Feels he is a genius...has no concept of the real world.  The class had no text and his tests and assignments were difficult and not helpful towards test preparation (easier than the tests).  You are either going to do very well, or very poorly, and no amount of studying will change the situation.

Sometimes trying to grasp the concepts was frustrating, but no pain, no gain, right?  Dr. Goddu was fun, engaging, and always willing to help.  He even hung out with my husband outside of class when he first came to U of R.

He is an interesting guy, but his class is SO hard!  He told us that some people "get it" and some people don't.  I did not.  I felt so lost and clueless and ended up with an awful grade.  Take Finite Math instead.

He's a little odd, but he's really funny and very smart.  He's also really helpful if you go see him outside of class.  Grading is hard to scale because logic is just one of those things that you get right or you don't, but he's pretty lenient with problem sets and VERY reasonable about homework.
Dr. Goddu is great! Very interesting and enthusiastic.

I couldn't stand this class.  He has absolutely no perception of anything that occurs outside the classroom.  He definitely knows what he is doing but seems to take pleasure in people failing rather than helping them achieve their goals.

He is rather smug in relation to his intelligence - he wants people to know that he's smart. That said, he's a good professor to those students who click with him. If the student-prof connection isn't there, though, it's certainly not worth the time.

Dr. Goddu is by far one of the best professors at UR.  Logic is not for everyone, but Dr. Goddu works with his students to help them understand the material.  I've taken 3 classes with him, and I wish I could take more!
Enjoys showcasing what a genius he is, has no text for the above class, confusing rhetoric, writing assignments are almost impossible and make you feel stupid.

Amazing.  The course is interesting and the work is consistent and not overbearing.  There is one section and one test everyone flops on, but Goddu has a way of keeping your hopes up with his quirky genius.
Really hard weekly assignments but you learn a lot if you do them.  Tests are ridiculously difficult too.  Goddu is a great professor though, and very enthusiastic.
Elementary Symbolic Logic is doable, but Goddu takes a certain delight in making us feel stupid with his weekly writing assignments. No attendance policy, but if you don't come, you're screwed.

One of the most interesting courses I have ever taken. I recommend taking any of his courses, for and intriguing and educational experience.  Although you do need to do your work, he makes the work enjoyable enough so that most times you don't mind.
Dr. Goddu is great--one of the best professors here.  I would highly recommend taking any of his classes.
